findings.reason: without one agreed figure set the completed-catalogue run cannot be read beside the partial one, which is the whole of section 10's measure.
findings.text: section 10 requires "the same counts as section 5 beside the partial run's" and then lists variables in each parse outcome, control-node groups, patterns under both keys and the share of component variables in a shared pattern, while section 5 (line 65) requires the fraction of the archive held, grouped and ungrouped counts, group-size distribution, the share of single-member groups and the twenty largest patterns with field counts; the two sets overlap only partly, so neither side can produce the comparison section 10 promises

findings.reason: the decision record is the durable evidence a later reader inherits, and as written it credits the local lane with a parse rate its own measurement reports as zero.
findings.text: the description-model decision states "the local model delivered 130 of 200 with no response parsing unrepaired", but the stored section 3 record gives the local lane 0 of 20 strict parses and 130 of 200 outputs against the paid model's 20 of 20 and 200 of 200; 130 counts delivered outputs, not responses that parsed

findings.reason: a worker on section 4 or 6 cannot tell whether ICP context is imported and passed to the chosen provider, and either answer changes what those sections deliver.
findings.text: the ratified rationale states "With ICP access parked, no ICP-derived content is in scope for it", yet section 4 delivers ICP and IDM content into the graph and section 6 (line 70) has that same paid model write component descriptions from the linked context of those nodes; the rationale and the two sections disagree about whether ICP content exists to be sent

findings.reason: section 4's dispatch either violates a stated gate or waits on a decision no one has been asked to make.
findings.text: the `local-lane-accepted` decision, whose context reads "Until then no ICP or IDM content is given to any worker", remains undecided while its face also names section 4 is the section that reads exactly that content, so section 4 is declared `implementable` under an open gate that forbids it
